Story
# 1

The golden curse brand sank inwards, evoking a resentful grunt from Aschetius. He clenched his fists tightly, the long shackles binding his arms rattling and clanking. The lava flowing around his perch bubbling up furiously with his change of mood, as if seething along with him, melting the rocks. Most of the time, Aschetius sits and seethes, his temperament unpredictable. Even his devotees are daunted by it.

# 2

Once a loyal vassal to the Dragon Queen, Aschetius now endures his volcanic exile — an eternity measured in molten centuries. The lizardfolk worship his dominion over flame and magma — yet their adoration rings hollow. His ambition burns singular: to reclaim his stolen divinity and escape this suffocating mortal realm. That these feeble creatures mistake him for a sun god — the irony would amuse, were he not so consumed by purpose.

# 3

In elder days, Aschetius bore little resemblance to the wrathful being he now embodies. His descent into this capricious malice stems from one singular torment — the theft of his power. To a soul that worshipped strength, no fate cuts deeper. Nor has he forgotten the architect of his ruin — that entity from chaos’ darkest gulfs who once laid him low. When regained power courses through his veins — should fate decree their paths cross anew — this time, the ending shall be rewritten.
